content:
The most anticipated television Emmy Awards kicks off this weekend, with the Creative Arts awards winners revealed first. The Primetime ceremony will be held on September 14, where top honors including Best Drama Series and Best Comedy Series will be handed out.

So far, Apple should be extremely pleased with the recognition, with its Apple TV+ leading the pack this weekend with a record-breaking 20 awards. The majority of that success comes from hit comedy Widows Bay, which took home 8 awards and is now the frontrunner for every top honor in the comedy categories.

The running tally for the 2026 Emmys so far has Apple in first with 20, HBO Max in second with 16, and Netflix in third with 13. The latter two streamers are expected to overtake Apple once the Primetime Emmys are all announced, but Apple is still safely in a respectable third place.

Apple is expected to dominate the comedy categories, but may fall short in drama to shows like The Pitt. The answers will be revealed next Monday.

To date, Widows Bay has won 8, Pluribus has earned 4, Margo's Got Money Troubles has taken 3, Palm Royale has also claimed 3, and documentary Mr Scorsese has brought home 1.

Those Apple TV titles account for 19 awards; Apple also won 1 for its ad "I'm Not Remarkable," which is how the headline number of 20 is reached:

Widow’s Bay

  • Best Guest Actress in a Comedy Series: Betty Gilpin
  • Best Production Design for a Half-Hour Program
  • Best Casting for a Comedy Series
  • Best Cinematography for a Half-Hour Series
  • Best Original Dramatic Score for a Series
  • Best Music Supervision
  • Best Sound Editing for a Half-Hour Comedy or Drama Series and Animation
  • Best Sound Mixing for a Half-Hour Comedy or Drama Series and Animation

Pluribus

  • Best Production Design for a Contemporary Program of One Hour or More
  • Best Editing for a Drama Series
  • Best Original Main Title Theme Music
  • Best Sound Mixing for a One-Hour Comedy or Drama Series

Margo's Got Money Troubles

  • Best Contemporary Costumes for a Series
  • Best Contemporary Hairstyling
  • Best Contemporary Makeup (Non-Prosthetic)

Palm Royale

  • Best Choreography for a Scripted Program
  • Best Period Costumes for a Series
  • Best Period or Fantasy/Sci-Fi Makeup (Non-Prosthetic)

Mr. Scorsese

  • Best Documentary or Nonfiction Series

Apple TV entered this season with a record-breaking 89 Emmy nominations, and it remains to be seen how many of those can be converted into trophies at the Primetime Emmy ceremony on September 14. All of this once again underscores the high praise industry critics have given to Apple's overall programming lineup.
